headline: Broad rotation beneath technology weakness
summary: US headline indices fell as large technology stocks weakened, but equal-weight and small-cap gains suggest rotation rather than broad liquidation. Earnings-related AI spending concerns remain the main near-term risk.

highlights.title: Participation is stronger than the headline
highlights.text: The equal-weight S&P 500 gained 1.20% and the Russell 2000 rose 1.01%, despite technology-led index declines. The report does not interpret this as a confirmed market-wide sell-off.

highlights.title: AI spending and earnings are the pressure point
highlights.text: Alphabet weakness and reported Amazon and Intel after-hours declines renewed concerns about AI investment returns. After-hours moves remain pending, not confirmed next-session closing outcomes.

highlights.title: A cautious, range-led original outlook
highlights.text: The report gives the base case 45%, with downside risk at 33%. Breadth and credit resilience argue against treating weaker technology futures alone as proof of systemic stress.

forecast.horizon: 30 October–3 November US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Embedded original US outlook, section 9. ID is an archive locator, not an author-issued forecast ID. issued_at is the verified completed Drive modification time; precise original issue time is unavailable. forecast.watch_next: Watch whether earnings-related losses narrow at the close, semiconductor confirmation, breadth and credit. The report's mean Brier is 0.725 across seven completed US windows, worse than its 0.667 uniform baseline.

limitations: Curated from the source report, not a new independent market verification. Put/call and current fund-flow data were unavailable. Oil settlement was media-reported, not directly checked with ICE; the January Brent settlement was missing. Several upcoming-event dates were not reverified with primary sources. After-hours prices remain pending.
